decision: OPEN-4 (condition verification) stops using finite condition-phrase enumeration as the primary gate. Replaced with: source claim -> cheap deterministic condition evidence + semantic condition-suspicion classifier (source-only, no compiled IR) -> ConditionSuspicionResult (NO_MATERIAL_CONDITION_SUSPECTED | MATERIAL_CONDITION_POSSIBLE | UNCERTAIN, with typed evidence spans/categories, provider/model/promptVersion/telemetry) -> routing policy -> deterministic trust gate.
routingPolicy: Independent semantic review runs when ANY of: deterministic inventory finds condition/exception/proviso evidence; classifier returns MATERIAL_CONDITION_POSSIBLE or UNCERTAIN; source/IR structural mismatch; any other existing verifier escalation condition. The only no-review path: deterministic reconciliation clean AND classifier explicitly NO_MATERIAL_CONDITION_SUSPECTED AND no other escalation condition. Classifier failure/throw/timeout ALWAYS routes to review, never skips it.
costDiscipline: Order: deterministic checks first; if they already require reviewer, skip the classifier call (no wasted spend); if deterministic alone would skip review, THEN call semantic suspicion as the second gate before allowing skip. Cache keyed on {tenant, document/source identity, source span hash, algorithm version, prompt version, model/provider} - no cross-tenant leakage.
independenceRule: The classifier receives ONLY source text, never compiled IR - it audits the compiler, so it cannot be handed the compiler's own output.
certificationStandard: Can novel material conditionality reach the independent verifier WITHOUT the exact drafting phrase being pre-enumerated in code? If no: FAIL, regardless of test pass rate. Manual code inspection required at recertification time, not just test-score trust.
productRuleGoverningAllSixFixes: The objective is not perfect parsing of English. It is: when Headroom does not have enough evidence to trust a contractual claim, it must know that it does not have enough evidence. Failing to fully understand a novel condition is acceptable; silently deciding there is no condition because its wording was unfamiliar is not.
